newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: US urges UN rights forum to stop picking on Israel.
newsitem.headline: US urges UN rights forum to stop picking on Israel.

text.p: The United States on Thursday urged the main U.N. human rights body to stop clogging its agenda with anti-Israeli resolutions and recognise that the Middle East peace process was working.

"We believe beyond a shadow of a doubt that the progress that has been made in that process has significantly benefited the human rights of the people most directly involved," Claiborne Pell, a former Senator from Rhode Island and senior member of the U.S. delegation to the U.N. Human Rights Commission said.
"The commitment of the United States to the Middle East peace process is well-known and unshakeable".
Pell accused the Commission of being "mired in the mud of old thinking" when discussing Israel, the only country subject to a separate agenda item in the annual six-week forum.
"Again this year we see the same old anti-Israeli resolutions coming to the floor, clogging our agenda with the same, tired old clichs of yesterday," he said.

Pell appealed to the 53-member forum to recognise major progress since the 1991 Madrid peace talks, including a drastic drop in the level of confrontation between Israelis and Palestinians in the West Bank and Gaza.
But he conceded human rights remained a problem in the West Bank and Gaza, and also in areas under Palestinian control.
Israelis and Palestinians were approaching the most difficult set of issues, negotiations on the permanent status of Jerusalem, due to begin next week, Pell said.
"We should not interfere with this process -- and make their task more difficult -- by kibitzing (meddling) from the sidelines".
Israel was a functioning democracy which had embraced peace with Egypt and Jordan, according to Pell, a former chairman of the powerful U.S. Senate Foreign Relations Committee.

"Israel has also engaged in a political process with Palestinians that has already given them control over their lives in Gaza and many parts of the West Bank, including most Palestinians in those areas -- and with more to come."

Hardline Arab states are expected next week to again present resolutions condemning Israel for violations in the occupied Arab territories, according to diplomats. U.S. officials told Reuters they planned to offer their own "balanced" resolution.

Pell said Israel was "doing the very thing this Commission has always wanted it to do -- taking difficult positions for peace, building ties of commerce and mutual interest with countries throughout the region and working for a comprehensive settlement of a conflict that has wracked the region for generations."
